newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Hydrous ups share of Brazil CS alcohol output.
newsitem.headline: Hydrous ups share of Brazil CS alcohol output.

text.p: Hydrous alcohol accounted for a larger proportion of all alcohol produced in Brazil's center-south region to June 1 than last year, independent consultants DataNet-Agricommodities said.
Of the 1.73 million cubic meters of alcohol output to the start of this month, 72 percent was hydrous and 28 percent anhydrous alcohol it said in a report.
Last year to the same period, the percentages were 67 percent and 33 percent respectively, DataNet said.

Center-south alcohol stocks were estimated at 1.34 million cubic meters - 978,000 cubic meters hydrous or around two months' consumption and 360,000 cubic meters of anhydrous alcohol which is sufficient for one month's consumption.
At the same stage last year, center-south stocks were only sufficient for 15 days' consumption both of hydrous and anhydrous alcohol.
According to DataNet, alcohol production to June 1 was 30.08 percent up on the same stage last year, while sugar output of 1.23 million tonnes showed a rise of 32.26 percent.
Sugar cane output of 32.90 million tonnes was up 19.12 percent on 1996/97 but DataNet is still expecting a overall growth of only between four and six percent this year.
Of the 1.23 million tonnes of sugar produced to June 1, around 95 percent was of crystal sugar, DataNet said.
Center-south sugar stocks on June 1 were estimated at 575,647 tonnes, 71 percent of which were in Sao Paulo state.
Around 69 percent of sugar sold to June 1 was directed to the domestic market and 31 percent to the export market.

The arbitrage between sugar and alcohol prices favored sugar sales to the domestic market up until the middle of May but then shifted to favor sales of sugar overseas and also sales of hydrous alcohol thanks to a increase in hydrous alcohol prices as of May 21, DataNet said.
Domestic and overseas sugar prices are nominally lower than last year, it added.
In the third week of June, average prices for crystal sugar in Sao Paulo state were 12.82 reais ($11.98) per 50-kg bag, ex-factory, tax paid, down 20.12 percent from prices last year.
